title: The query profile db write parses every profile a second time
body:
`write_mmseqs_profile_database` in `mmseqs.rs` writes the mmseqs query db for hmm queries. It walks the queries with `P7Hmm::iter`, which parses each profile with `Profile::from_p7hmm` from the mapped file. For each match state it writes 20 scores, as bits times 8 cast to `i8`, then the consensus residue twice and three zero bytes. It runs on one thread, right after the target db write, and the "db write" leaf of the `-s` tree times both.

`build_pipeline` in `search.rs` already parsed the same profiles into an `Arc<Vec<Profile>>` before seeding starts. The writer parses them all a second time.

On 20,795 Pfam profiles against 2,455,940 targets at `-t 8`, the db write leaf took 7.31 s, against 4.32 s with one profile. That puts the profile db at about 3 s. The figure is a difference between two runs and was not timed on its own.

## Proposal

Pass the profiles `build_pipeline` built to the writer, so nothing parses them twice. Build each profile's bytes in parallel, then write them in order and assign the offsets in one pass, as nail-fc2ac4 proposes for the target db. The two writers can also run side by side.

## Open

- Whether the `Arc<Vec<Profile>>` reaches the seed stage without changing `Pipeline`'s layout.
- Sequence queries take a different path, `write_mmseqs_sequence_database`, and are not part of this issue.
